sub_types.online_platform_sellers: HMRC has data from platforms (eBay, Vinted, Etsy, Airbnb and others) under the digital platform reporting rules, in force from 1 January 2024.
sub_types.missed_return: A return HMRC expected was not received (ITSA6).
sub_types.other_income: Other campaigns, e.g. overseas income, property income, crypto.

not_this_letter_if: the letter opens a compliance check (CC/FS1a, CC/FS22 or similar): route to the accountant

facts_for_explanation.what_it_is: A 'nudge' letter is HMRC asking you to check that your tax is right, because it has information suggesting you may have income you haven't declared. It is not a penalty and not a formal investigation, but you should not ignore it.
points: If you only sold your own used belongings for less than you paid, that is usually not trading and not taxable.
Trading income up to £1,000 a year can be covered by the trading allowance.
If you do owe tax, telling HMRC yourself usually means lower penalties than if HMRC finds it later.
Platforms report sellers to HMRC once they make 30 or more sales, or about £1,700 or more, in a year. Being reported does not by itself mean tax is due.
facts_for_explanation.threshold_check: Confirm the 30 sales / €2,000 (about £1,700) reporting threshold before launch

routes.if_respond_by_date_within_14_days: highlight the date and offer a call-back

future_link: Online seller tax checker (Vinted/eBay/Etsy/Airbnb uploads, £1,000 trading allowance, badges of trade) will start from this letter type.
